headline: Sensex and Nifty crash as relentless foreign fund outflows trigger longest weekly losing streak in 25 years

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Relentless foreign fund outflows and mass selling by foreign investors
Global rate hikes and rising oil prices sparking significant capital outflows
Longest weekly losing run in 25 years dampening domestic investor sentiment

whatHappening: Sensex dropped 570 points at closing after an intraday crash of 1,000 points
Manufacturing PMI rose to a seven-month high of 55.1 in September
Commercial LPG cylinder prices were increased by ₹65
Passenger vehicle wholesales grew in double digits in September despite market volatility
summary:
Indian benchmarks recorded their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years as relentless foreign fund outflows wiped out trillions in market value.
Despite a seven-month high in manufacturing PMI and strong auto sales from TVS Motors, the Sensex plummeted over 570 points.
Global factors including rate hike fears and rising oil prices continue to pressure domestic equities.
